newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower on spreads, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower on spreads, exports.

text.p: CBOT nearby soy products ended sharply lower, pressured by unwinding of bull spreads amid a bearish export outlook, traders said.

The fundamental outlook was disappointing, marked by news South Korea and Taiwan snubbed U.S. supplies to buy cheaper South American supplies and ideas a cold, wet spring would delay corn plantings and force farmers to plant more soybean acres.
Taiwan overnight bought 54,000 tonnes South American soybeans while South Korea bought 85,000 tonnes Brazilian soymeal.
The sales confirmed ideas South America would take a dominant role in exports as harvest there progressed and prices fell.
New-crop months were pressured by forecasts for cold, wet weather across much of the U.S. Midwest next week.
Bear spreads were the featured trade in soymeal. Rosenthal Collins spread 200 lots August/May at $13.00, premium May, LIT America spread 200 lots August/July at $8.90, premium July.
Soymeal ended $4.60 to $0.90 lower, with May off $4.60 at $282.80 per ton. Soyoil settled down 0.23 to 0.16 cent, with May 0.16 cent lower at 24.00 cents a lb.
Trade sources said U.S. exports will probably fall sharply in the coming months as world buyers rely on abundant South American supplies.

News several private analytical firms were lowering their projections for Brazilian and Argentine soybean output drew little attention. Traders said reports of drought damage had been in the market for weeks and damage reports were in line with expectation.

"It's still a huge crop, folks," said Dale Durchholz, analyst with Agrivisor Services, a division of the Illinois Farm Bureau. "Brazil has shown that they're going to be a formidable exporter of beans and meal. There's a good potential that they can put a pretty serious dent into demand for U.S. soybeans this spring and into summer."
On the day, Cargill Inc bought 500 lots July soymeal, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer and ING each bought 300 lots July and 100 May and Smith Barney bought 200 lots July and 50 May.
Merrill Lynch sold 500 lots May and 300 July while ADM sold 200 July and 100 December, pit sources said.
In soyoil, ADM bought 300 lots May and 100 July, Refco Inc sold 100 May and 50 July and Merrill Lynch sold 100 July, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 20,000 lots, compared with Monday's actual volume of 22,877 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 8,000 lots, against Monday's 10,641 lots.
